question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Surat — Location & European Presence]
options: Surat is located on the western coast of India in present-day Gujarat
Surat lies near the mouth of the Tapti (Tapi) River
The English established their first factory in India at Surat in 1608/1613
Surat is located at the mouth of the Narmada River
wrong_fact: Surat is NOT at the mouth of the Narmada. It stands at the mouth of the Tapti (Tapi) River. The Narmada empties into the Gulf of Khambhat (Gulf of Cambay) further north near Bharuch (Broach), which is a separate city.
explanation: Surat is situated on the southern bank of the Tapti River in Gujarat, about 20 km from its mouth in the Gulf of Khambhat. The English captain William Hawkins arrived in 1608 and Thomas Best's victory over the Portuguese (1612) led to the first permanent English factory at Surat in 1613. Surat was India's premier port before Bombay's rise.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Surat — Trade & Mughal Context]
options: Surat was the principal port of the Mughal Empire and the embarkation point for Hajj pilgrimages
The Dutch also established a factory at Surat in the 17th century
Shivaji sacked Surat twice — in 1664 and 1670 — plundering its wealth
Surat was directly administered by the Portuguese from 1612 onwards as part of their Estado da India
wrong_fact: Surat was NEVER directly administered by the Portuguese. After the Battle of Swally (1612), the English defeated the Portuguese and gained Mughal favour, establishing their factory. Surat remained under Mughal sovereignty throughout the 17th century. The Portuguese controlled pockets on the nearby coast (Daman, Diu) but not Surat city.
explanation: Surat was the Mughal Empire's chief port for international trade and the departure point for Hajj ships (Surat-Mocha route). The Dutch set up a factory there in 1616. Shivaji's raids of 1664 and 1670 were famous plundering expeditions. The Battle of Swally (1612) ensured English, not Portuguese, dominance at Surat under Mughal permission.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Surat — Decline & Bombay's Rise]
options: Surat's commercial importance declined after the English shifted their western India headquarters to Bombay in 1687
The English headquarters on the western coast was transferred from Surat to Bombay partly because Bombay offered a superior natural harbour
Bombay was received by England as part of the dowry when King Charles II married Catherine of Braganza in 1661
Surat declined because it was captured and permanently annexed by the Maratha Empire in 1687
wrong_fact: Surat was NOT permanently annexed by the Marathas in 1687. The English East India Company transferred its western headquarters from Surat to Bombay in 1687 for commercial and strategic reasons (Bombay's superior harbour). While Shivaji raided Surat (1664, 1670), the Marathas did not 'permanently annex' it — Surat remained nominally under Mughal authority before gradually coming under British control.
explanation: Bombay was ceded to England by Portugal in 1661 as part of the dowry of Catherine of Braganza's marriage to Charles II, and later leased to the EIC for £10 per annum. Bombay's deep natural harbour, defensible island location, and freedom from Mughal interference made it ideal. The EIC moved its Surat Presidency headquarters to Bombay in 1687. Surat's decline was commercial, not due to Maratha annexation.
